name: Ngorongoro Crater
tagline: The world's largest intact volcanic caldera, a natural amphitheatre holding black rhinos, lions and 25,000 large animals.
highlight: Descending into the crater at dawn and finding a black rhino in the mist.
shortDescription: A UNESCO World Heritage caldera 600 metres deep and 20 kilometres wide, with dense wildlife, flamingo lakes and Maasai communities on the rim.
metaDescription: A Ngorongoro Crater travel guide: the crater floor, rim lodges, black rhinos, Olduvai Gorge, Empakaai, Maasai culture, costs, tips and a two-day plan.
nearestAirport: Kilimanjaro (JRO) or Arusha (ARK), about 3 hours by road from Arusha
budget: US$300-800+ per person per day, safari

image.file: File:Ngorongoro Crater - view of the crater.jpg
image.alt: The vast green floor of Ngorongoro Crater seen from the rim

intro: Ngorongoro Crater is what remains of a giant volcano that collapsed some two to three million years ago, leaving a caldera about 20 kilometres across with walls rising 600 metres. The floor holds grassland, a soda lake, swamp and forest, and a permanent year-round water supply that keeps a remarkably dense collection of animals in place.

About 25,000 large animals live in the crater, including lions, hyenas, elephants, hippos, buffalo, wildebeest and zebra, and it is one of the best places in Africa to see the endangered black rhino. Lake Magadi hosts flamingos at times. Because the crater walls act as a natural enclosure, game viewing is excellent in any season.

The Ngorongoro Conservation Area is a multi-use area, where Maasai pastoralists still graze their herds on the highlands. The crater rim sits at about 2,300 metres, so nights are cold and misty. Most visitors descend for a half-day game drive from a lodge on the rim, and the area also includes Olduvai Gorge, a key site in the study of early humans, and the Empakaai Crater.

gettingThere.intro: Most visitors arrive by road from Arusha.

options.text: About 3 to 4 hours to the rim.
options.detail: Usually part of a safari circuit.

options.mode: Fly to Lake Manyara or Serengeti

gettingAround.intro: Inside the conservation area you will need a 4x4 and a guide.

options.text: Only with a ranger on the rim.

bestTime.headline: June-September
bestTime.summary: Dry months give the easiest roads and the best visibility, though the crater is good year-round.

seasons.text: Dry, cool and good viewing, but busier.
Warm, with fewer visitors and many calves.
Long rains, mist and lowest prices.

bestTime.avoid: April and May, when mist and mud can limit visibility.

itinerary.title: Two days at Ngorongoro
itinerary.intro: A rim lodge and one game drive.

days.title: The rim
days.morning: Drive from Arusha and stop in Karatu
days.afternoon: Check in at the rim lodge

days.title: Into the crater
days.afternoon: Picnic lunch by the hippo pool
days.evening: Return to Arusha or continue to the Serengeti

tips: Dress in layers, since the rim is cold and misty.
Book a lodge on the rim for the views.
Descend early, as vehicle numbers are limited by time.
Keep window sills clear and stay in the vehicle.

faq.a: A half-day in the crater, plus an overnight.

faq.q: Can I walk into the crater?

faq.a: Most say yes for the density of wildlife.

faq.q: Can I combine it with the Serengeti?
faq.a: Yes, it is on the usual route.
